title: Privacy policy
description: How Yuppers.app collects, uses, shares and keeps information about the people who use Yuppers.
note: This policy describes how Yuppers.app works today.

blocks.p: This policy explains how Yuppers.app (https://yuppers.app) collects and uses your information. Yuppers.app (“we”, “us”) runs Yuppers, a service for writing, signing and keeping track of two-person agreements, called yups, on the website yuppers.app and in the Yuppers app. Below we explain what information we collect, how we use it, who sees it, how long we keep it, and the choices you have.
Yuppers is offered in the United States, to adults 18 and over, in English and Spanish. Our servers and our database are in the United States.
Using Yuppers is also governed by our {terms}.
For any question or request about your privacy, write to {privacyEmail}.

what-we-collect.title: What we collect and how we use it

blocks.p: We collect what Yuppers needs to work, and use it only to run Yuppers. For each kind of information below, we say what it is and how we use it. We don’t use analytics, advertising or tracking tools, and we don’t build profiles of you. We do not sell your personal information. We do not share your personal information or your SMS opt-in data and consent with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

ul: Your email address, your phone number, or both. We send one-time sign-in codes to them, we email you when something happens in one of your yups, and, if you turn on text updates for an agreement, we text your phone number when its status changes.
Your name, as you want the people you make yups with to see it.
Your language (English or Spanish), so that the product, our emails and our codes reach you in it.
That you confirmed you are 18 or over, and when. We don’t ask for your date of birth.

When your account was created, and your sign-ins: how you proved it was you (a code by email or by text message), when, and until when each one lasts. We use these to keep you signed in, and to end your sign-ins when you sign out or delete your account.

What you and the other person write and do in each yup: its terms; each item, with what is given, how much, by when, and how you’ll both know it’s done, including any amounts of money you name; the names of both people as the proposal gives them; every version sent; messages, notes and statements; each signature; and what each of you records about delivery. Keeping this is the point of Yuppers: it is the shared record of what you agreed and what happened.
Drafts you are still writing. We save them as you go so that you don’t lose them.

What you tell us about the other person. Whoever writes a proposal gives both people’s names, and may give the email address or phone number the invitation is for. We use that address only to check that the person who opens the invitation is the one it was meant for. We never send anything to it.

blocks.p: When you sign, we record your account, how you proved it was you (a one-time code by email or text message) and when, the time you signed, a fingerprint (hash) of the exact terms you signed, and which version of the consent wording you were shown, in which language. We also record the IP address your request came from and the description your browser or app gives of itself (its user agent). These are evidence of the signature. The IP address and the user agent are deleted after {networkDays} days, and the app never shows them to anyone; the rest of the signature stays with the agreement.

If you report a yup or a proposal, we keep your report: the reason you chose, what you wrote, who sent it, and which yup and person it is about. We use it to review the report and act on it. If you block someone, we keep who you blocked and when, and use it to keep that person out of yups with you. When a report is reviewed, we keep a history of what the reviewers looked at and decided, to keep review accountable.

blocks.h: Text updates for an agreement, if you turn them on

blocks.p: If you turn on text updates for an agreement, we keep a record of it: which agreement, the phone number, when you turned them on, and the consent wording you were shown. We use it only to send you those updates and to show that you agreed to receive them.

blocks.h: Notifications in the app, if you turn them on

blocks.p: If you turn on notifications in the Yuppers app, we keep your device’s push token, its platform (iOS or Android), the app’s version and your language, so that we can send notifications to that device.

blocks.h: Wallet passes, if you add one

blocks.p: If you add a yup to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet, we keep a record of the pass: which yup and account it belongs to, and how it was last updated. For Apple Wallet we also keep the identifiers and push tokens that Apple gives us for the devices that hold the pass, so that we can keep it up to date. A pass shows the yup’s reference code, its status, how many items are still to do, and a link back to the yup. It never shows the terms, names or amounts.

ul: Request logs. For each request our service answers, we log the method and the path (never the query string), the status, how long it took, and a request ID. We use them to run the service and to find and fix problems. Our logs never contain what was sent or answered, codes, tokens, email addresses, phone numbers or IP addresses.

Sign-in limits. To stop anyone from guessing codes or asking for too many, we count the codes asked for from each IP address and the wrong codes entered for each email address or phone number. These counts are stored under a keyed hash, never the address or the number itself.

One-time codes. We store a keyed hash of each code we send, never the code itself, with the email address or phone number it went to and when. We use these to check the code you enter, and to limit how many codes are sent.

cookies-and-storage.title: Cookies and storage on your device

blocks.p: The website uses one cookie and two pieces of browser storage, all to make the product work. There are no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies, and no scripts from anyone else.

ul: yuppers_session (a cookie): keeps you signed in. It holds a random token, lasts {sessionDays} days or until you sign out, and the page’s scripts can’t read it.
yuppers.language (local storage): the language you picked, so that the website opens in it next time.

yuppers.invitation (session storage): the code from an invitation link while you sign in to read it, so that reloading the page doesn’t lose it. It is removed once the invitation is opened or turns out to be no longer valid, and when you close the tab.

blocks.p: In the Yuppers app, your sign-in is kept in your device’s secure storage (the iOS Keychain or the Android Keystore), with your notification setting for that device. A copy of a record that you choose to share is kept in the app’s cache only until you make the next copy or sign out.

Besides you, your information is seen by the other person in each yup, as far as the yup shows it; by the people who review reports, while a report is open; and by the companies that help us run the service.

blocks.h: The other person in a yup

blocks.p: The other person sees what the yup shows: its terms, every version, the messages and notes, its history, the signatures and when they were made, and your name as the agreement gives it. They don’t see your email address, phone number, IP address or device. Each of you can download or print the yup’s record, and what each of you does with that copy is up to you.

Reviewers we name can see a report, the names and account status of the people it involves, and the whole record of the yup it is about, but only while the report is open. Every report a reviewer opens, and every decision, is written to a history that can’t be changed. Nobody reviews a report they are part of.
The people who run Yuppers can also reach the database directly, to operate and back up the service and to answer requests like yours.
We use these companies to run Yuppers. Each receives the information needed for the job described:

ul: Render hosts our service, our database, our server logs and the database’s backups, in the United States.

Cloudflare runs our domain’s DNS and carries every request to yuppers.app over its network before it reaches Render, so it handles your IP address and the request. It may ask your browser to report connection errors to it. It also forwards email sent to our addresses, such as {privacyEmail}.
Postmark sends our emails, so it receives your email address and the email: a one-time code, or a notice that something happened in one of your yups (which never includes the terms).
Twilio, when we send text messages, receives your phone number and the message: a one-time code or, if you turned them on, an agreement update.

Expo, Apple and Google, if you turn on notifications in the app: Expo receives your device’s push token and the notification and passes them to Apple’s or Google’s push service, which delivers it. A notification only says “Your yup has an update.”, with the yup’s internal ID so that the app can open it.
Apple and Google, if you add a Wallet pass: Apple delivers the pass’s updates to your devices, and Google keeps the pass (its status, reference code and number of items) to show it in Google Wallet.

blocks.p: We don’t share your information with anyone else, except where the law requires us to. We don’t sell it, share it for advertising, or let anyone use it for their own marketing.
When we offer them, Yuppers.app sends text messages in two programs, and for nothing else: no marketing.

ul: Yuppers.app sign-in codes: a one-time code to sign in (which also creates your account the first time), or to confirm that you want to delete your account. We send one only when you ask for a code, and only to the number you entered or, to confirm a deletion, the number on your account. Entering your number and asking for a code is your request for that text. Message frequency: one message for each code you ask for.

Yuppers.app agreement updates: if you turn on text updates for an agreement, by ticking a box on that agreement, we text you when its status changes, for example when the other person signs, marks something delivered, confirms it, disputes it, or asks to close it. Message frequency varies; there is no fixed maximum: one text per status change of an agreement you turned updates on for. An update says only that something changed, with a link to sign in and see it. It never includes the terms, amounts or names of goods, just as our emails and app notifications don’t.
Message and data rates may apply.

**Reply HELP for help.** **Reply STOP to stop receiving texts from us.** STOP stops all texts from Yuppers.app, sign-in codes included, so you’ll need to sign in with an email address instead. Turning off text updates for one agreement stops the updates for that agreement only.
Phone numbers outside +1 are not texted: we send texts only to numbers that start with the country code +1.
We do not sell your personal information. We do not share your personal information or your SMS opt-in data and consent with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
Mobile information will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
Mobile information and opt-in consent are not shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
To deliver the texts, we give your phone number and the message to our SMS provider, Twilio, and to no one else.
Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.

blocks.p: For help with text messages, write to {supportEmail} or reply HELP to any of our texts. For privacy questions, write to {privacyEmail}. The terms of both programs are in our {terms}.

ul: Your email address, phone number, name and language: while you have an account. Deleting your account removes them at once.

Yups that were sent, with everything in them and their history: we keep them as the shared record of what was proposed and agreed. We don’t delete them when one or both people delete their accounts, and we have not set a time after which they are deleted.
Drafts you haven’t sent: until you send them, discard them or delete your account.
The IP address and user agent recorded with a signature: {networkDays} days.

One-time codes: each code works for {codeMinutes} minutes, and only once. We don’t yet delete the records of codes (the hash, where it went and when) on a schedule; deleting your account deletes the ones for your email address and phone number.
Sign-ins: each lasts {sessionDays} days, unless you sign out first.
Sign-in limit counts: two days.
Push tokens: until you turn notifications off, sign out on that device or delete your account, or the push service tells us the token no longer works.

Wallet passes: the record of a pass stays with its yup; when you delete your account, your passes are voided. The device identifiers Apple gives us are removed when a device removes the pass, and no later than 30 days after a pass is voided.

Reports, and the history of how they were reviewed: kept, including after an account is deleted, so that leaving doesn’t erase a complaint. Blocks you make: until you unblock the person or delete your account.
Server logs: kept by our hosting provider, Render, for up to 30 days.

Backups: our hosting provider keeps copies of the database for recovery for up to 7 days, and we may keep our own backup copies for a limited time. If we ever restore a backup, we first delete again every account that was deleted after the backup was made, so a deleted account stays deleted.
The deletion log: when an account is deleted, we keep its account ID and the time, and nothing else, so that a restored backup can’t bring it back.

blocks.p: You can delete your account yourself, at any time, from your account page on the website or in the app. To confirm it’s you, we send a one-time code to your email address or phone number that only works for deleting your account. Deleting can’t be undone.

ul: You’re signed out on every device.
Your email address, phone number, name and language are removed from the account.
Your one-time codes, the devices registered for your notifications, drafts you haven’t sent, notifications waiting to be sent to you, and your list of people you’ve blocked.
Invitation links you made that nobody used stop working, and forget the address they were for.
Your Wallet passes are voided.

blocks.h: What happens to yups that are still open

ul: A draft you haven’t sent is discarded.
A proposal waiting to be signed ends with nothing agreed.
An agreement in progress gets a request to close, made in your name. The other person is told and has time to respond, and then it closes as unresolved.

Yups that were sent stay with the other person, as the record of what was proposed and agreed: the terms, the history, your signature, and your name exactly as the agreement gives it. Your name in those records is not removed or replaced.
The IP address and user agent recorded with your signatures, until {networkDays} days after each signature.
Reports you made, or that were made about you, and the history of their review.

An account record with no contact details and no name: its ID, when it was created and when its holder confirmed being 18 or over, which the signatures it gave rely on; and its line in the deletion log.
Backup copies, until they expire as described above.

blocks.p: You can sign up again later with the same email address or phone number. That is a new account, with none of your old yups.

ul: See your information: your account page shows your email address, phone number, name and language, and each yup shows everything in it, with its whole history.
Correct it: you can change your name and language on your account page. A name changed there is used from then on; agreements already sent keep the names they were written with.
Take a copy: you can download each yup’s record as a file, or print it or save it as a PDF.
Delete your account: from your account page, as described above.

Notifications in the app: turn them on or off on the app’s account screen, or in your phone’s settings. Emails about your yups are how we tell you that something needs you, so there is no setting to turn them off; we never send marketing emails.

blocks.p: For anything you can’t do yourself, such as changing your email address or phone number, getting a copy of your information or asking a question about this policy, write to {privacyEmail}. We may need to confirm that a request comes from you before we act on it.
Residents of some states may have additional rights under their state’s laws. You can make any privacy request at {privacyEmail}, and we will respond.

Yuppers is only for adults 18 and over. Everyone confirms that they are 18 or over when they set up their account, and nobody can sign a yup without that confirmation. We don’t knowingly collect information about anyone under 18. If you think someone under 18 is using Yuppers, report it from the yup (“Someone under 18 is involved”) or write to {privacyEmail}.

ul: Connections to Yuppers are encrypted (HTTPS), and browsers are told to use nothing else.
We store one-time codes, sign-in tokens, the codes in invitation links and Wallet tokens only as hashes, never as they are.
The service uses a restricted database account that can add to an agreement’s history but can’t change or delete it, and the database itself refuses changes to that history.
Only reviewers we name can see reported yups, only while the report is open and after signing in within the last 12 hours, and every report they open is recorded.
Our logs leave out personal information such as email addresses, phone numbers, codes and tokens.

blocks.p: No system is perfectly secure, and we can’t promise that information will never be reached by someone who shouldn’t have it. If you think your account has been misused, write to {privacyEmail}.
When the way Yuppers handles information changes, we update this policy and post the new version on this page, with a new effective date at the top.
